top5.title: Anthropic jumps 34% in its IPO debut
top5.description: Anthropic shares jumped 34% in their first trading session, pushing the AI company’s valuation above $2 trillion.
top5.why: Anthropic’s IPO debut, with shares surging 34% and valuation exceeding $2 trillion, signals that public markets are strongly validating—and potentially amplifying—the AI investment boom.

top5.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon, its new flagship model
top5.description: Google has launched Gemini 4 Neon, a model positioned between Carbon, its most powerful model, and Hydrogen, its faster and cheaper option. Neon ranks third on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and is available in AI Studio, the Gemini API, Antigravity, and the Gemini app for paying Pro and Ultra subscribers.
top5.why: Google’s Gemini 4 Neon strengthens the competitive frontier-model race and gives enterprises and developers another high-performing option across Google’s rapidly expanding AI ecosystem.

top5.title: The Java4Shell flaw exposes widely used enterprise applications
top5.description: Oracle has patched a Java vulnerability that allowed unauthenticated attackers to execute code or crash vulnerable systems. Researchers demonstrated attacks against Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Elasticsearch, with exposure depending on the Java version and processor configuration.
top5.why: The Java4Shell vulnerability threatens widely used enterprise systems such as Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and Elasticsearch, making immediate exposure assessment and patching a priority.

top5.title: OpenAI says its models improved AMD chip designs by 14%
top5.description: OpenAI says its models improved the power, performance and area of AMD chip designs by up to 14%. AMD incorporated some of the changes into a design sent for manufacturing.
top5.why: OpenAI’s reported 14% improvement to AMD chip designs suggests AI-assisted hardware engineering is becoming commercially useful and could reshape competition in the semiconductor supply chain.

top5.title: Washington speeds up exports of Nvidia H200 chips to China
top5.description: According to The Information, the head of the Bureau of Industry and Security reportedly pushed to quickly approve H200 sales to China. These sales, authorized in December 2025, provide for 25% of the revenue to go to the U.S. government.
top5.why: The reported acceleration of Nvidia H200 exports to China, with the U.S. taking 25% of sales revenue, could materially affect chip markets, U.S.-China technology policy, and Nvidia’s growth.
